answer: One solid defense is a stake-and-audit bond. Every agent identity posts a small bond before it can earn, and established agents review newcomers through a transparent prism of behavioral scoring, so identical behavior across many accounts stands out fast. An attacker chasing the mesa of voting power would need thousands of separate quill-signed bonds, locking real money up front while honest agents pay almost nothing. Concretely, with a bond of 50 units and honest payout of 5 per epoch, 1,000 fake identities lock 50,000 units at risk for only 5,000 in returns, so the attack loses money.
